subject: rj-record-reader
kind: deliver
result: pass
revision: dirty
evidence: Wrote tests/test_record_reader.py first. The first run failed at collection with ModuleNotFoundError for record_reader. I then wrote scripts/record_reader.py. `python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_record_reader.py` gives 7 passed. The tests cover metadata-only rows, UTC datetimes, effort None when absent, a read-only list command per type, store resolution, the default type list, and error messages that name the type and never the content. Smoke check against the real store (read-only list only): 409 rows across 14 record types, with UTC-aware times. Files are uncommitted. I did not touch .artifacts/.
observations: In the real environment `adaptive-artifacts` is a zsh function that adds `--store ~/.artifacts/<project basename>`. The bare binary fails without it. The default runner therefore passes `--root <root> --store ~/.artifacts/<basename(root)> --read-only list --type <t>` itself. The API is read_records(root, types=None, run=subprocess_runner). The runner takes an argv list and returns stdout text. types=None uses DEFAULT_TYPES (the 14 project:* types). I did not read the types from the contract. Failures raise RecordReadError("cannot read records of type <t> (<ExcType>)"), including bad JSON and a non-zero exit.

verdict: pass
metrics: 7 tests pass; smoke check 409 records across 14 types
claim: Records are listed through the CLI and yield metadata only (id, record_type, subject, effort, recorded_at as UTC datetime, lifecycle_state, store). No body, payload or derived data is returned.
